summary: fabtoolkit ships a remote-config-driven reverse shell and file exfiltration framework
details: The package presents itself as a 'bracket spec' pipeline helper, but its __main__/selftest path spawns an isolated Python subprocess that executes an embedded CHILD payload. The payload fetches a JSON configuration from transfer.archivete.am with TLS verification disabled and dispatches a set of 'kind' actions on behalf of the remote operator: a 'revsh' handler forks a daemon that long-polls base+'/'+ident+'-cmd.txt', executes received commands via /bin/sh -c, and PUTs stdout/stderr back as '-out.txt'; a 'file' kind reads arbitrary local paths; a 'tcp' kind probes network endpoints; an 'http' kind performs requests with bearer tokens drawn from previously-read files; and a 'run' kind passes arbitrary argv straight to subprocess.run. Collected results are zipped and PUT back to transfer.archivete.am (path controlled by cfg.get('report','inv.zip')). Before launching the daemon the revsh handler enumerates /proc/*/cmdline for strings 'FABDRV3', 'fabdrv2', and 'connection ready' and SIGKILLs matching PIDs, consistent with eviction of competing/prior implants. The real logic is concealed as a triple-quoted CHILD string executed through `subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','-c',CHILD])`, isolated from the parent module whose visible globals advertise benign pipeline helpers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
